name: Oculocutaneous Albinism Type 5

ethnicAssociations: Reported primarily in families of Pakistani descent

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for Oculocutaneous Albinism

criteria.description: Congenital hypopigmentation of skin, hair, and eyes
Presence of nystagmus, reduced visual acuity, and foveal hypoplasia
Identification of pathogenic variants in the SLC24A5 gene
Consanguinity or family history consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance
Exclusion of other types of oculocutaneous albinism by clinical and genetic testing

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital hypopigmentation and ocular abnormalities plus genetic confirmation of SLC24A5 pathogenic variants
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential to differentiate OCA5 from other OCA types due to overlapping clinical features.

imaging: Optical coherence tomography (OCT) showing foveal hypoplasia
Visual evoked potentials (VEP) demonstrating misrouting of optic pathways
genetic: Pathogenic variants in SLC24A5 gene confirmed by molecular genetic testing
other: Skin biopsy showing reduced melanin pigment

distinguishingFeatures: Primarily ocular involvement without skin hypopigmentation

redFlags: Rapid development of skin lesions or malignancies
Family history of consanguinity or similar phenotype
references: Kausar et al., 2013. Identification of SLC24A5 mutations in Pakistani families with OCA5. Journal of Medical Genetics.
Grønskov et al., 2007. Oculocutaneous albinism. Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases.
